workloads.consumer: inference request, model-load or rendering-frame helper owner
workloads.task: Discover 32 Status-bearing helper tasks while processing one owner, stop admission, retain the first business failure and drain every helper before owner teardown.
workloads.lifecycle: One persistent four-worker Scheduler serves 64 warmup and 1024 measured owners. Each owner creates all helper coroutine frames, admits them dynamically, lets every helper yield once, validates every output, aggregates one failure in roughly one of sixteen owners and tears down all ownership before the next owner.
workloads.semantic_equivalence: The candidate uses TaskScope::add so scope-only Status helpers do not manufacture unused result handles. The pre-v7 migration baseline composes the public SpinLock for concurrent admission/close, a public CancelToken that can be passed into cancellable IO, spawn_task, one same-allocator PMR vector of JoinHandle<Status>, every-handle join and first-Status retention. Both use the same Task<Status> body, allocator, scheduler, group-cancellation visibility, cooperative yield, output slots, failure distribution and full-drain completion boundary; all per-owner ownership setup and teardown is charged.
workloads.negative_space: This is not detached fire-and-forget, a fixed compile-time when_all pack, a bare WaitGroup counter, an admission-unaware handle vector, a worker-stack callback or an IO/backend latency benchmark.
